outcome: Admission to neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: Women under 35 years old who became clinically pregnant after fresh blastocyst transfer (n=545)
finding: Double blastocyst transfer (DBT) was associated with increased multiple pregnancies, Cesarean sections, prematurity, decreased fetal anthropometric measurements, and NICU admissions without an increase in live birth or reduction in abortion rates compared to elective single blastocyst transfer (eSBT).
mod_finding: DBT was associated with increased Cesarean section rates compared to eSBT.
